description: SortBy orders records by a numeric key and keeps ties in list order
code:
tasks = [{name: "ship", due: 3}, {name: "plan", due: 1}, {name: "test", due: 3}, {name: "build", due: 2}]
agenda = tasks.sortBy(task -> task.due)
agenda.map(task -> task.name)

description: SortBy compares string keys as text, by code point
A negated key sorts numbers in descending order
code:
scores = [{name: "ana", points: 9}, {name: "bo", points: 3}, {name: "cy", points: 7}]
scores.sortBy(score -> -score.points).map(score -> score.name)

description: A sorted declaration follows its list while the list keeps its own order
code:
queue = [{id: 1, eta: 30}, {id: 2, eta: 10}]
route = queue.sortBy(stop -> stop.eta).map(stop -> stop.id)
queue.push({id: 3, eta: 20})
assert(route, [2, 3, 1])
queue.map(stop -> stop.id)

description: SortBy orders a class population and follows new instances and changed keys
code:
class Runner(name, time):
    this.name = name
    this.time = time
board = Runner.sortBy(runner -> runner.time)
ana = Runner("ana", 31)
Runner("bo", 28)
ana.time = 25
board.map(runner -> runner.name)

description: A class-level rule ranks every instance by its place in a sorted population
code:
class Bid(who, amount):
    this.who = who
    this.amount = amount
$Bid.place = Bid.sortBy(bid -> -bid.amount).indexOf($Bid) + 1
ada = Bid("ada", 40)
bo = Bid("bo", 65)
cy = Bid("cy", 50)
[ada.place, bo.place, cy.place]

description: A key that is not set yet leaves the sorted list null until it is set
code:
class Job(name):
    this.name = name
queue = Job.sortBy(job -> job.due)
press = Job("press")
press.due = 5
coat = Job("coat")
assert(queue, null)
coat.due = 2
queue.map(job -> job.name)

description: A selector error rolls back the change that triggered it
code:
labels = ["b", "a"]
sorted = labels.sortBy(label -> label.toUpperCase())
failure = ""
try:
    labels.push(7)
catch error:
    failure = error
[failure, labels.length, sorted]
